behavior: GET /api/tasks return JSON list of tasks. Superseded by F11: now returns a paginated envelope {content, totalElements, totalPages, page, size} instead of a bare array, since filtering/sorting/pagination was added to this same endpoint.
evidence: GET /api/tasks returns {"content":[{"id":1,"title":"init-check",...}],"totalElements":1,"totalPages":1,"page":0,"size":20}. Response contract changed by F11 (see F11 evidence); old bare-array contract no longer applies.

behavior: Data persist across restarts (H2 file mode)
verification: restart app, GET /api/tasks still contains the task created previously
evidence: Restarted app after init.sh run; GET /api/tasks still returned [{"id":1,"title":"init-check"}]. DB file at ./data/tasks.mv.db

behavior: POST /api/tasks/import accepts a JSON array of tasks, bulk creates them, returns 201; imported tasks persist across restart
verification: curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/tasks/import -d '[{"title":"x"},{"title":"y"}]' | grep '201'; restart app; GET /api/tasks still contains imported tasks
evidence: POST /api/tasks/import with [{"title":"imp1"},{"title":"imp2"}] returned 201 [{"id":2,"title":"imp1"},{"id":3,"title":"imp2"}]; empty array [] returned 201 []; [{"title":""}] returned 400; after app restart, GET /api/tasks and GET /api/tasks/2 still returned the imported tasks

behavior: GET /api/tasks/{id} returns full task detail, 404 if not found
Every request produces one structured JSON log line with a requestId correlation id, echoed back as the X-Request-Id response header
verification: curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/tasks -H 'X-Request-Id: test-corr-id'; confirm response header X-Request-Id: test-corr-id and a JSON log line containing "requestId":"test-corr-id", "status":200
evidence: curl -i /api/tasks -H 'X-Request-Id: test-corr-id' returned header X-Request-Id: test-corr-id and log line {"...","message":"method=GET path=/api/tasks status=200 durationMs=120","logger":"com.example.taskapi.config.RequestLoggingFilter","level":"INFO","requestId":"test-corr-id"}; request without header got an auto-generated UUID echoed back and logged; GET /api/tasks/999999 (404) logged at WARN with its own requestId. Full ./init.sh run passed with all log lines in JSON.

behavior: Every TaskService method (listTasks, getTask, createTask, importTasks) logs one structured JSON line per outcome: INFO on success with identifying context (task id/count), WARN for not-found/invalid-input with the offending input and reason, ERROR for unexpected exceptions with the exception and enough context to diagnose without full task titles/bodies. All lines correlate with the request's requestId via MDC.
verification: Exercise each method's success and failure paths (GET /api/tasks; GET /api/tasks/{id} valid id and missing id; POST /api/tasks valid and blank title; POST /api/tasks/import valid array, empty array, array with an invalid element) and confirm one business-level JSON log line per case, correct level (INFO/WARN/ERROR), matching requestId to the access-log line, and enough context (task id / offending input / exception) to diagnose without re-running the request
evidence: Exercised each TaskService method's success/failure paths with distinct X-Request-Id headers: listTasks -> "listTasks success count=0" (INFO); createTask -> "createTask success id=33" (INFO), and the @Valid blank-title 400 case produced no service-level line (validation happens before TaskService, matching the access-log WARN); getTask -> "getTask not found id=999999" (WARN) and "getTask success id=33" (INFO); importTasks -> "importTasks success count=2" (INFO), "importTasks success count=0" for [] (INFO), "importTasks invalid element index=1 reason=blank_title" (WARN). Every line's requestId matched the corresponding RequestLoggingFilter access-log line. Also verified via full ./init.sh run.

behavior: GET /api/tasks?category=&status=&sortBy=&sortDir=&page=&size= filters (category, status combined with AND, both optional), sorts (sortBy: title|createdAt|category, default createdAt; sortDir: asc|desc, default desc), and paginates (page default 0, size default 20) tasks. Invalid sortBy/sortDir -> 400 with a clear message, no crash. Filter combination yielding 0 results -> 200 with empty content array. Response includes pagination metadata {content, totalElements, totalPages, page, size}.
verification: Create tasks with varying category/status via POST /api/tasks and /api/tasks/import; exercise GET /api/tasks with: no params (defaults), category only, status only, category+status combined, each sortBy value asc/desc, page/size, an invalid sortBy, an invalid sortDir, and a filter combo yielding 0 results. Confirm response shape, ordering, pagination fields, 400 on invalid sortBy/sortDir, and empty content array (not an error) on 0 results.
evidence: Created tasks with category/status combos (work/open, work/done, home/open, ops/open). GET /api/tasks (no params) -> paginated envelope, defaults sortBy=createdAt sortDir=desc page=0 size=20. ?category=work -> 2 matching tasks; ?status=open alone -> 3 matching tasks; ?category=work&status=open -> AND-combined to 1 task; ?category=nope -> 200 {"content":[],"totalElements":0,"totalPages":0,...} (no error). Verified sortBy=title/category/createdAt each with asc, and default desc; page=0 vs page=1 (size=2) returned distinct, correctly-ordered slices with consistent totalElements/totalPages; combined category+sortBy+sortDir+page+size in one request also correct. ?page=-1 -> 400 "page must be >= 0"; ?size=0 -> 400 "size must be >= 1". Verified GET /api/tasks/{id}, POST /api/tasks, POST /api/tasks/import still work with new category/status fields, and restart-persistence holds with the new schema. ./check_architecture.sh passes (0 violations). During self-review against evaluator-rubric.md, found and fixed a real defect: ?sortBy=bogus / ?sortDir=bogus returned 400 with NO message in the response body (Spring's server.error.include-message defaults to 'never'), failing the spec's 'trả 400 kèm message rõ ràng' requirement -- fixed by adding server.error.include-message=always to application.properties; reverified 400 bodies now include the actual reason text, and confirmed this didn't regress F06's 404 or the existing @Valid blank-title 400. See evaluator-rubric.md for the full scored self-review (4.0/5, average of 5/5/5/1/4 -- test coverage is 1 since there are no automated tests anywhere in this project, only manual curl+log verification). Note: ./init.sh's hardcoded `sleep 15` before the health check is flaky on this machine independent of this change -- reproduced the same timeout on unmodified HEAD via git stash before/after this work, so it is a pre-existing environment timing issue, not a regression; build, health check, and all feature checks pass when run manually with a longer startup wait (~18-20s).
